events.subject: Choose tools beyond the screwdriver
events.preview_text: Check whether 64 bits and practical handling tools fit the repairs you want to attempt.
events.body:
Prepare for different kinds of electronics work with one organized repair kit. The iFixit Pro Tech Toolkit combines a **64-bit driver set** with tools for opening, prying, gripping, and anti-static handling.

That distinction matters when comparing toolkit breadth. A larger bit count expands the fasteners you can approach, but bits alone do not cover the other steps a repair may involve.

The Pro Tech Toolkit also includes an assortment of tweezers, spudgers, opening tools, and anti-static safety accessories. Its stated device range spans electronics, gaming consoles, drones, RC cars, and vintage devices.

The useful question is not simply whether you need 64 bits. It is whether that bit range and the additional repair tools match the device categories and repair steps you expect to encounter. The product page lets you inspect both before choosing.

events.subject: Give removed screws a workspace
events.preview_text: The case lid becomes a sorting tray while the tools stay organized.
events.body:
Give removed screws a dedicated surface while you work. The iFixit Pro Tech Toolkit lets you use the inside of its driver-kit lid as a sorting tray during disassembly.

The lid attaches magnetically to the driver-kit case. Remove it, turn it over, and you have a defined place to arrange fasteners instead of treating the case as packaging that sits aside.

When the work is done, the magnetic case and foam insert provide secure tool storage. The included fabric roll makes the broader toolkit portable, so the same design supports work at the bench and carrying the tools elsewhere.

A sorting surface does not record where each screw belongs, so careful tracking still matters. Visit the product page to decide whether the integrated tray and organized storage fit the way you want to work.
events.call_to_action: See the case and storage design

events.message: Email 2, draft 1: "Put the case to work"
events.subject: Put the case to work
events.preview_text: The magnetically attached lid provides a sorting tray for removed fasteners.
events.body:
The iFixit Pro Tech Toolkit puts part of its driver-kit case to work during disassembly. The inside of the magnetically attached lid serves as a sorting tray for fasteners as they come out.

That gives removed screws a defined work surface instead of leaving the case useful only for storage. You still choose how to group and track each fastener for reassembly.

When the work is done, the magnetic case and foam insert provide secure tool storage. The included fabric roll makes the broader electronics repair toolkit portable.

The product page shows how the sorting-tray lid, case, foam insert, and fabric roll work together—so you can decide whether this storage design belongs in your repair workflow.

edits.line: Give removed screws a dedicated surface while you work. The iFixit Pro Tech Toolkit lets you use the inside of its driver-kit lid as a sorting tray during disassembly.
edits.problem: The product is named but never plainly identified, so a stranger must infer that it is a general electronics repair toolkit.
edits.fix: Orient the reader in this opening paragraph with one plain category sentence while keeping the sorting-tray use as the paragraph's point.

edits.line: The lid attaches magnetically to the driver-kit case. Remove it, turn it over, and you have a defined place to arrange fasteners instead of treating the case as packaging that sits aside.
edits.problem: This repeats the headline and opening paragraph, delaying the storage payoff without adding enough new information.
edits.fix: Retain only the concrete lid-removal mechanism and its use during disassembly; remove the repeated packaging contrast.

edits.line: When the work is done, the magnetic case and foam insert provide secure tool storage. The included fabric roll makes the broader toolkit portable, so the same design supports work at the bench and carrying the tools elsewhere.
edits.problem: The second sentence drifts into an unestablished bench-versus-travel scenario and uses the vague phrase “same design,” which weakens the central transformation from work surface back to storage.
edits.fix: Tie the case, insert, and roll directly to returning and carrying the organized toolkit after the tray has been used, without assigning the reader specific work locations.

edits.problem: The generic greeting and human-style sign-off sound like a competent stranger rather than the company's direct, punchy campaign voice.
edits.fix: Remove the conversational framing so the message opens directly on the repair use and closes on the single CTA.

events.subject: A place for removed fasteners
events.preview_text: The magnetic lid serves as a sorting tray, then returns to organized storage.
events.body:
A toolkit case can be useful before cleanup begins. The iFixit Pro Tech Toolkit is a general electronics repair kit with a driver-kit lid designed to support disassembly.

The lid attaches magnetically, and its inside serves as a sorting tray. Once removed from the case, that surface provides a place to arrange fasteners as they come out.

After the repair, the magnetic case and foam insert provide secure tool storage. The included fabric roll keeps the organized toolkit portable, returning the lid from a working surface to part of the stored kit.

The tray does not record each fastener’s original position, so careful tracking still matters. The product page shows how the lid, case, foam insert, and fabric roll work together, helping you decide whether that design belongs in your repair setup.
